title: Entitlements catalog
summary: Diceroll's License → Entitlements page: the catalog moved out of Managed config, with the three kinds (on/off, quantity, consumable) and each one's combine rule, a tier-by-entitlement view with the add-ons that give each key, and the platform entitlements, each shown only while its feature is on.
compare: The page lives in the Licensing group (Licenses, Tiers, Add-ons, Entitlements) of the Product context, in the License accent; there is no Licensing Settings page and no entitlement table left in Managed config's catalog.

Three kind tiles explain the one rule per kind in plain words: an on/off entitlement is off unless the tier, the license or any add-on turns it on; a quantity is the license's value, else the tier's, plus every add-on; a consumable is units with a balance and a ledger per license. The UI calls kind `feature` 'On/off', never 'Feature', which names the six features (C-58).

Each catalog row shows the label, the key in mono (what the code asks for), the kind, the value per tier in list order (Free, Premium), and the add-ons that give it as links to their records. A pack-gating key says which pack it opens. An on/off value reads 'On' with a tick or 'Off' in muted text; '—' appears only where no value can exist (a consumable's tier cells, an empty Add-ons cell).
Quantities show numbers per tier and the add-on's '+2'; consumables show no tier values (units come only from add-ons).

Platform entitlements are a separate, read-mostly table: Release tracks (channels) under Ship builds, Versions (app.minVersion/maxVersion, set in the tier's Duration or on a license), Device limit and Tier (license.tier/tierLabel, locked, set by Polaris Key) under Licensing, Cloud Sync storage (pkey.cloudSync.bytes) under Cloud Sync, each with the feature's glyph in its accent and where it can be set.
Turning off Ship builds or Cloud Sync removes its row here and in the tier and add-on editors without deleting values; test by toggling the feature on Settings and reloading this page.
The footer explains the composition order (tier, license overrides, add-ons, platform keys) and that devices keep receiving flag rows, so no SDK code changes (C-09).
Words: 'Entitlement', 'Add-on', 'Release tracks', 'Limits'; never 'flag', 'grant' or 'capability' in the UI.

Phone: the sidebar folds into the menu button, the kind tiles stack, the filter becomes a full-width segmented control, the tables drop their header row, and each row keeps its label and key with one summary line that starts with the kind's icon and names tiers and add-ons apart ('On in Premium · add-on Obsidian dice pack'), add-ons as links; nothing scrolls sideways.

The section says what editing does to a declared entitlement: 'Edit one here and the console owns it from then on: later changes to the file won’t touch it.' Saving an edit to an entitlement declared in .pkey/product asks first ('No ads is declared in .pkey/product. After this, resyncs leave it as you set it here.') with the button 'Save and stop following the file'.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fix, then pass: the kind is now 'On/off', so 'Feature' keeps its one glossary meaning; the file-ownership copy says exactly what happens, and the phone rows read cleanly.

findings.issue: The word 'Feature' means two things: the on/off entitlement kind (tile, filter, Kind column, add-on record) and, in the Platform table's column, the glossary's six features.
findings.resolution: Renamed the kind to 'On/off' in the tile, the filter (All · On/off · Quantities · Consumables), the Kind column, the phone summaries and the add-on record's rows; the identifier stays `feature`. The Platform table's Feature column keeps the glossary meaning. For the lead: add 'On/off' to the glossary (integration.md §2) under Entitlement as the UI word for kind `feature`.

findings.issue: 'Editing one here claims it from the file' is jargon and hides whether a later resync overwrites the edit; the add-on record's save hint never mentions the file.
findings.resolution: The section now says 'Edit one here and the console owns it from then on: later changes to the file won’t touch it.' The add-on record's save bar says the same for that add-on, and the compare specifies the confirmation on saving a declared entitlement, whose button repeats it: 'Save and stop following the file'.

findings.issue: The Gems row links a '3,000 gems' add-on that the Add-ons page (8 add-ons) doesn't have.
findings.resolution: Removed 3,000 gems from the row and from the phone summary; the add-on count stays 8.

findings.issue: The em dash means 'off' for on/off entitlements and 'not applicable' or 'none' elsewhere.
findings.resolution: On/off cells now read 'Off' in muted text. '—' remains only where no value can exist: the consumable's tier cells and an empty Add-ons cell.

findings.issue: Phone: a header row holding only 'Entitlement', add-on names lose their links, a tier and an add-on run together in the summary, and Versions says 'Set on: Tier, license' although versions are set in the tier's Duration.
findings.resolution: The header row is hidden on phone. Summaries start with the kind's icon and name each part: 'On in Premium · add-on Obsidian dice pack', 'Free 2 · Premium 6 · Loadout pack +2 · Neon dice pack +1', with every add-on a link. Versions' Set on reads 'Tier duration, license' on desktop and 'set in the tier’s Duration' on phone.
